reasoning: The pipeline's rule is that a shown result closes the work and the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery. A row whose definition of done names his eye as the check is only describing one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserve for him — a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a still-open fork in the definition of correct. This work is none of them: the delivered page shows what the plan holds and nothing else, no part of it is a matter of preference, and it reaches nothing past what was ordered. The observable outcome — every plan row appearing live on the standing board page — is decided by a command and a plain read: scripts/render-board.sh regenerates board.html, tests/test_board_matches_the_canon.py passes against the generated page, and the page was opened and renders as described. So the acceptance line is a misdescription of an ordinary buildable result, not one of his reserved cases, and waiting on his look would be leaving a row open for him to bless what was already shown. The pipeline verifies through a check that did not produce the work, and because the done names a rendered surface (page/board.html) the receipt must carry --surface board.html, not the fixture alone; then it clears IN PROGRESS and NEXT, closes the checkpoint in the same step, shows the result and continues. If he disagrees after seeing it, that is a new fact and its own task; this row stays closed.
